archetype: Azorius draw-go control: gift the whole table cards, convert the gift into a per-spell discount through the flipped Heliod, act only at instant speed behind a pillow fort and eight counterspells, and win with the second cast of Approach of the Second Sun. The commander is the converter, not the threat: Heliod, the Warped Eclipse reads 'You may cast spells as though they had flash. Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn' (oracle text, cards.json), so the discount is largest on the opponents' turns, which is exactly where a flash deck spends its mana. Twenty generic-cost artifacts (enumerated from cards.json) are the cards that discount all the way to free; the three cards that changed for v1.3.0 (Isochron Scepter, Horn of Greed, Mind Stone) are all three of that kind. deck-facts finds one contained combo line (Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 15, produces 'Win the game') and two_card_infinites: 0. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's Walser distinction is the one the pilot named himself as commander dependence HIGH: 'built around your commander is not reliant on it. A deck whose only payoff sits in the command zone hands three opponents one target' - here the PAYOFF (Approach) does not sit in the command zone but the CONVERSION does.

role_assignment.default_role: Control that owns the long game outright. strategy:whos-the-beatdown gives Duke's test - 'who has inevitability? — whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown' - and strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock names its sources: 'superior late-game card quality, an engine that scales, an unanswerable finisher, or simply more answers than the opponent has threats.' This deck holds the last two: Approach's second cast from hand wins on resolution (verified stack 002, checker.verdict == 'pass', which names the stack as the only interaction window), and 8 counterspells plus 21 interactive copies (deck-audit 'interaction' axis: 14 copies, verdict 'at' against 12-15). The measurement agrees with the assignment: on the 120-game Forge run on v1.2.1 (run b0f44e4a, 2026-09-09, pod 'standard'), heliod won 20 of 99 decided games (0.202, ci95 [0.135, 0.292] per diagnosis) and 12 of those 20 read won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'", 8 read 'all opponents have lost'; on the 40-game standard-v3 run (4b0e1964, same sha) 10 wins, 5 by Approach and 5 by outliving the table. You are never the beatdown by damage: combat damage dealt to players on the 120-game run had mean 3.28 and MEDIAN 0.5, noncombat mean 1.23 and median 0.0. The metagame-clock section's Commander correction is the deck's premise - 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan' - and the pilot's own operating description ('pass with everything untapped, do nothing in the main phase, act at instant speed') is strategy:multiplayer.pod-management's last sentence made into a build: 'Leaving instant-speed mana open forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction.'
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: The pivot is the second Approach and nothing else. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window sets the bar: 'The window opens when your win attempt either can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for — or doesn't need to resolve fully to leave you ahead.' Approach fails the second clause outright (a countered Approach goes to the graveyard, no life, no win check - stack 002 step 3, rule 701.6a), so only the first clause applies, and it has three concrete parts: the first Approach has resolved and sits seventh from the top; you have drawn or tutored it again (Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans, or the Scepter copying Mystical Tutor - the last is a candidate line, not a fact); and you can pay {6}{W} less the day's discount with a counter still up. Goldfish mean available mana crosses 7 at turn 8 (7.064; 6.412 at turn 7) with the discount OFF, so read that as the ceiling on how late it is. strategy:tempo.sequencing's Commander correction says where the cast goes: 'prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent' - a sorcery cast in that window needs the flipped Heliod's flash grant on the battlefield, which is why commander dependence is HIGH. Before the window opens, strategy:pivot-point's instruction is the entire plan: 'hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after'. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection prices the wait: 'The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out'. Log 002 records the failure mode in the pilot's own words - he sat on Long-Term Plans overthinking a cost that 'with the treasure and the discount ... is two or three, not seven', and the combo seat took its window first; strategy:resource-hedging names it: 'playing *scared* is paying real equity to dodge specific cards'.
role_assignment.seat_relative_note: strategy:whos-the-beatdown's Commander correction: 'role is seat-relative — you can be the beatdown against one opponent and the control against another in the same turn cycle; assign per-threat, not per-game'. On the 120-game run giada-angels caused 43 of heliod's 61 eliminations (8+11+11+13 across seat positions) and all 61 were eliminated_how 'damage' - against the flier seat you are pure defence and the fort is the whole game. Against the two grinding seats you are the one accruing, and strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's Rice rule holds your one-for-ones in hand: 'hold removal until the threat is pointed at you, and let opponents spend their one-for-ones on each other.' Against a combo seat (log 002, cause 'combo') the assignment flips to strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's exception: 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now'.

candidate_missing_lines.title: How big the discount is on an opponent's turn: draw step + Howling Mine + Horn of Greed land drop + Font of Mythos
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The back face counts 'each card your opponents have drawn this turn' (oracle text). On an opponent's turn their draw step is one, Howling Mine's upkeep trigger is a second, a land drop under Horn of Greed a third, Font of Mythos two more - so a {2} artifact such as Mind Stone or the Scepter should be free from the second draw. This is the mechanism every v1.3.0 swap was argued on (branch.json) and nothing in stacks/ has resolved a single discounted cast; the goldfish cannot model it at all.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The second Approach at an opponent's end step under Heliod's flash grant, with Fierce Guardianship held

Whether Fierce Guardianship's free mode is live in that window depends on Heliod still being on the battlefield - Forge b0f44e4a transformed him in 44 of 120 games.

A Scepter copy of Mystical Tutor at each opponent's end step would repeat that for {2} without spending a card, which would make the three-card 'Win condition access' group (0.495 assembled) effectively wider. If both readings hold, the live imprint set is eleven, not thirteen, and the pilot should never imprint either. A rules question for the resolve-stack loop, not a strategy claim.

matchup_frames.vs_the_standard_pod: MEASURED, on v1.2.1 not v1.3.0. Run b0f44e4a (Forge, 120 games, 4 seeded jobs, 600s clock, pod 'standard': giada-angels / baylen-tokens / abaddon, all bracket 3), seat sha 214af3084f80: heliod 20 wins of 99 decided (20 truncated, 1 drawn), win_rate 0.202, ci95 [0.135, 0.292] per diagnosis, against the table's null of 0.180; the diagnosis reads the -0.050 against the earlier 120-game run as 'NOT a decline' (Newcombe ci95 [-0.1614, +0.0644], MDD 0.185). Run 4b0e1964 (standard-v3: sythis-enchantress / jarad-graveyard / abaddon, 40 games, same sha): 10 wins of 35 decided, win_rate 0.286 - forty games cannot separate that from anything (CLAUDE.md: MDE 42 points at 20 games/arm). STALENESS: both runs describe the list three cards ago; the diagnosis's own phrase 'on the sleeved list' was true when written and is not now. deck-info marks diagnosis.stale = true. Nothing Forge-measured exists for Isochron Scepter, Horn of Greed or Mind Stone, and the goldfish reads none of them (branch objective was a CONTROL, damage_8 >= 0.0).
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The matchup that kills you, and it flies: giada-angels caused 43 of heliod's 61 eliminations on b0f44e4a and all 61 were 'damage'; combat_damage_taken mean 37.92, median 31, against combat damage dealt mean 3.28, median 0.5. strategy:combat-math.racing's Commander correction rules out the race: 'you cannot race three life totals — races there are two-player subgames run while the rest of the table develops'. So you do not race; you tax and you block, and strategy:card-advantage.virtual says which is worth more per slot: 'one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once'. The tax layer (Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes) assembles 0.496, 0.357 by turn six - the least reliable of the four defensive groups; the block layer is five fliers and zero reach at 0.68 / 0.529, one of which (Kefnet) cannot block below seven cards in hand, and it lost a body (Angelic Wall) to Mind Stone in v1.3.0 on the argument that 'the taxers plus twelve counterspells are the defence' (branch.json) - a count this frame cannot reproduce (eight, see disagreements). strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's caster-side reading is the fallback: two wraths and a Rift, cast when 'another player's board be the reason it gets cast'.
matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Your board is not your plan, so a rival wrath costs you the fort, not the win: creatures_lost and first-attack figures on the Forge runs show a deck that barely commits (combat dealt median 0.5). The danger is the counter war on the Approach turn, and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's standard is written for you: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing.' Stack 002 makes the constraint exact - the stack is the only window and a countered Approach yields nothing. strategy:information.range-tells is the read on the other blue seat: 'Held lands plus instant-speed pace means interaction until proven otherwise' and 'what they did NOT do with mana available is the strongest signal'. Log 001 is the recorded loss to this: 'I countered a spell, Alex countered my counter; I cast Swords to Plowshares, Alex redirected it onto Heliod', cause 'removal'. The Scepter imprinting Swan Song or Dovin's Veto is the v1.3.0 answer to a counter war (a counter every turn for {2}) - unmeasured, and the activation is undiscounted.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Structurally the worst matchup, and strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial says why: 'Decks built on many cheap spells per turn are hit hardest: taxes attack the velocity math directly, so recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine.' This deck's curve is 22 twos and 18 threes (deck-facts), and its whole edge is casting at a discount; a Sphere effect is the discount in reverse and a Rule of Law / no-flash piece blanks the back face. The section forces the role: 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion' - for a deck whose only clock is a seven-mana sorcery cast twice. Outs by class (strategy:combat-math.probability: 'play around *classes* of effects (a wrath by turn six, some counterspell behind blue mana) rather than named cards'): Disenchant, Cathar Commando, Loran of the Third Path, Cyclonic Rift, Force of Negation and Dovin's Veto on the way in; deck-audit breadth covers artifact (4) and enchantment (4) but graveyard and land are uncovered (3 of 5 classes, verdict 'under'), and strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite warns 'a counter answers a lock piece only on the way in, so some answers must be castable under the tax'.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Log 002 is the recorded loss (cause 'combo'): 'Oliver assembled his one-card Cranko line while the table beat on me.' strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy carries the correction to this deck's usual restraint: 'The countervailing risk: held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now'. Eight counterspells (two free) are the right tool and strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's 'counterspells do both jobs' is why the same eight cannot all be held for the Approach turn; strategy:threat-assessment's Commander correction re-ranks the table for you: 'draw engines, ramp bursts, combo proximity, and board *quality* outrank board quantity; re-rank every turn instead of fixing on one player'. The gift is the risk here - Forced Fruition was cut for handing a combo seat seven cards a spell (branch.json), and Horn of Greed still draws that seat one card per land. strategy:multiplayer.pod-management's pacing rule is the frame: 'engines want the game slow until the pivot window' - the combo seat wants it fast, and the table's tempo is the thing to fight over, not its life totals.

overall_assessment: This deck builds a board to not die behind, and wins with a card that says you win. The world-view is strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's - 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds' - and the deck owns the long game on two of that section's four sources, an unanswerable finisher and more answers than the table has threats. The mechanism is an inversion the doc only half-covers: eleven permanents hand the whole table cards, which reads as generosity (strategy:multiplayer.politics, strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's 'engines that read as defensive'); the flipped Heliod then bills each of those draws back as {1} off your spells and lets you cast them at instant speed, so the deck does nothing on its own turn and everything on theirs (strategy:multiplayer.pod-management: 'Leaving instant-speed mana open forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction'). v1.3.0 leans harder into that: all three new cards are generic-cost artifacts that discount to free, and the Scepter turns one of thirteen cheap instants into a per-turn ability the discount does not touch. The measurement says the theory is right about HOW the deck wins and wrong about how OFTEN: on 120 Forge games (v1.2.1) it took first 20 times against a null of 0.180, 12 by Approach and 8 by outliving the table, dealing a median 0.5 combat damage; the diagnosis's verdict stands - 'Nothing about this deck's mana flow or card flow is what limits it; conversion is' - and the conversion has one hub. Forge transformed Heliod in 44 of 120 games; the goldfish puts the flip at 0.561 by turn six; log 001 lost him to a counter war and a redirected Swords, log 002 to the pilot's own Supreme Verdict. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's line is the whole finding: 'built around your commander is not reliant on it. A deck whose only payoff sits in the command zone hands three opponents one target; buy it back with redundant copies' or 'protection' The payoff is Approach; the CONVERSION is Heliod, and the five-card insurance package is the buy-back, with Leyline of Anticipation the only redundant copy of the flash half and nothing at all duplicating the discount half. Two honest holes. First, strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density asks for 'at least 3 finishers' and this is a one-finisher deck by the pilot's standing choice, whose fallback is attrition - which on the same run won 8 games to Approach's 12. Second, the fort is the least reliable of the four defensive groups (0.496 assembled, 0.357 by turn six) while the gift is the most reliable (0.898, mean turn 2.639): for several turns a game the deck is handing three opponents cards from behind a door that is not yet locked, and all 61 of its eliminations were damage. The posture risk is the one strategy:resource-hedging opens on - '"playing not to lose" prioritizes delaying defeat over maximizing win probability, and it is mathematically wrong' - and log 002 shows the pilot paying it ('I was overthinking the mana cost ... I waited, got desperate, and the window closed'). The section's rule is the correction: 'hedge from ahead, gamble from behind', and the pivot window 'still demands full commitment the turn it opens'.

gaps: NO SECTION ON COST REDUCTION AS A RESOURCE. The query 'artifact ramp mana rocks cost reduction free casts' tops out at strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base (0.483), which is about land counts. This deck's entire v1.3.0 argument - a per-spell discount that lives on opponents' turns, generic-cost cards as free casts, activated abilities excluded - has no home. Wanted: how to value a conditional discount against a rock, why a discount favours cheap generic costs over coloured pips, and the difference between reducing a spell and paying an ability.

NO SECTION ON REPEATABLE-EFFECT ARTIFACTS (Isochron Scepter and its class). The query 'Isochron Scepter imprint repeatable counterspell value' returns nothing above 0.146. Wanted: what a repeatable {2} counter or tutor is worth per turn cycle against three responders, which imprints are live, and the tell it hands the table.

NO SECTION ON ALTERNATE WIN CONDITIONS. A 'you win the game' card is not a threat: it cannot be blocked, raced or removed once resolving, and the entire skill is one window on the stack. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window comes closest and is written for board-based kills ('Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail'), which Approach cannot do. Wanted: the two-cast structure (Approach, Thassa's Oracle, Test of Endurance) as a class, how many tutors and protection slots one is worth, and timing across three responders.

NO SECTION ON SYMMETRICAL RESOURCE GIFTS. The query 'group hug symmetric card draw feeding opponents Howling Mine' peaks at strategy:card-advantage.virtual (0.331), which is about blanking cards. Wanted: when the gift is net-positive, the conversion rate that makes it so, and the failure mode where the cards you handed out kill you (log 002, a combo seat).

NO SECTION ON PILLOW-FORT / DETERRENCE ECONOMICS. One clause in strategy:card-advantage.virtual is the whole of it; 'pillow fort tax attackers Propaganda Ghostly Prison deterrence' tops out at 0.278. Wanted: how many taxers make a deterrent rather than a speed bump, {2}-per-attacker against tokens versus Voltron, and why an untaxable route breaks the layer.

NO SECTION ON THE DRAW-GO POSTURE. The measured gap is interaction in hand 0.929 versus castable 0.61 at turn six; strategy:multiplayer.pod-management has one sentence on open mana and strategy:tempo one marker on unspent mana. Wanted: how much mana to leave up across a four-player turn cycle and when to break posture and develop.

NO SECTION ON EVASION AXES AND BLOCKER COVERAGE. The deck spent five slots on fliers off a measured 43-of-61 elimination count from one seat and had no framework to size that against; 'aggro go-wide fliers racing three opponents' returns strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry (0.547), which does not cover blockers.
